AC1 and AC2 reference 'CancelBackupCommand' but the CommunityToolkit.Mvvm-generated property is 'BackupCancelCommand' (convention: {MethodName}CancelCommand). All three artifacts (ViewModel attribute, AXAML binding, test assertion) consistently use BackupCancelCommand. WP-007 should document the correct property name in api-surface.md.

Edge-case: double-cancel is safe — CancellationTokenSource.Cancel() is idempotent and the token is already cancelled on the second call. Edge-case: cancel before IsBusy=true is prevented at the UI level (IsVisible={Binding IsBusy} hides Cancel button); even if triggered programmatically, the finally block keeps IsBusy=false correctly.

summary: IncludeCancelCommand = true on the [RelayCommand] attribute correctly enables source-generator emission of BackupCancelCommand — naming follows the CommunityToolkit.Mvvm {MethodName}CancelCommand convention.
finally { IsBusy = false; } is the correct idiom for ensuring state cleanup on cancellation, exception, and normal completion — no catch block is needed nor should be added.

AXAML bindings are clean: Cancel button uses IsVisible={Binding IsBusy} (appears only while busy), Backup button uses IsEnabled={Binding !IsBusy} (prevents double-submission), Close button has no IsEnabled binding (always enabled). Button ordering Backup → Cancel → Close is correct.

Test design for CancelBackupCommand_CancelsInProgressBackup is exemplary: TaskCompletionSource<> sentinel eliminates the race condition; TrySetResult() is defensive; Task.Delay(Timeout.Infinite, ct) is the canonical blocking-until-cancel pattern; OperationCanceledException catch-swallow is intentional and correct.
No blocking issues, no fix-forward changes applied, one documentation-forward tag recorded. PASS.

comments.note: After a successful cancellation the UI silently returns to 'ready' state (HasResult stays false, ResultMessage stays empty, Cancel button disappears). This is acceptable UX — the user explicitly pressed Cancel — but a 'Backup cancelled.' status message in ResultMessage would improve discoverability. Not blocking; worth considering as a follow-up product decision.
